newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Alan Bond pleads guilty in Australia's largest fraud.
newsitem.headline: Alan Bond pleads guilty in Australia's largest fraud.

text.p: Jailed entrepreneur Alan Bond on Wednesday pleaded guilty to two charges of dishonesty relating to the biggest corporate fraud in Australian history worth A$1.0 billion (US$800 million).
Bond, 58, already serving three years jail for fraud involving a French impressionist painting, faces a maximum five years jail for each of the new charges.

Bond admitted in the Western Australia Supreme Court that in 1988 and 1989 he failed to act honestly as a company director and acted with intent to defraud when he created a A$1.0 billion unsecured loan from Bell Resources to his ailing Bond Corp.

Prosecutor Michael Rozens said Bond pleaded guilty after the prosecution agreed to drop a further five charges relating to the Bell Resources fraud which followed Bond Corp taking control of the Bell Group Ltd in mid-1988.
Bond had pleaded not guilty to all charges and was to stand trial in April. He will reappear on February 3 when three days have been set aside for his plea in mitigation.
Bond was jailed for three years in August for fraud involving the French impressionist painting, La Promenade.

He was also jailed for two-and-a-half years in 1992 after being found guilty of inducing a former friend to contribute to the rescue of a Western Australia bank while concealing a A$16 million fee for his own company. He served only a few months in jail before a second jury acquitted him at a re-trial.
Bond was lauded as Australian of the Year after winning the prestigious America's Cup yacht race in 1983.
His personal fortune was estimated at A$350 million (US$273 million) in the late 1980s, before the collapse of his Bond Corporation Holdings Ltd under a pile of debt, totalling A$600 million.

Bond, a former signwriter who built a global network of companies with interests spanning mining, property, media and breweries, was declared bankrupt in April last year. But was freed of bankruptcy in February this year.
